### struct `SecretAttachment`

A reference to one secret attached to an agent — its scope (`project`, or `None` for a global secret) and key `name`. At launch, exactly the secrets in an agent's attachment list are decrypted and exported into the run's environment under their literal `name`s: an explicit **allowlist**, not the whole scope. Serialized as a TOML array-of-tables (`[[secrets]]`).

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SecretAttachment {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub project: Option<String>,
    pub name: String,
}
```

### struct `HarnessClaudeSdkArguments`

Arguments accepted by the `harness:claude-sdk` backend: the `claude` CLI run headless by ADI's harness. It shares the Claude engine knobs with the pty/process Claude backends, but adds a harness turn cap (`max_turns`) and the adi-mono command scope (`tools`), and drops the process-only options (`output_format`, `max_budget_usd`, `add_dir`).

### struct `HarnessAdiArguments`

### struct `Await`

```rust

pub struct Await {
```

### enum `Cause`

Why an await is being considered — and, when it wakes, what the run is told happened.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Cause<'a> {
    Event {
        name: &'a str,
        payload: &'a str,
    },
    Timer,
    Expired,
}
```

### struct `Woken`

One await that woke its conversation, reported back so the app can log it. `error` is set when the await was claimed but the reply itself failed — the wake is gone either way, which is why it is worth saying out loud.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Woken {
    pub id: String,
    pub agent: String,
    pub conv: String,
    pub cause: String,
    pub error: Option<String>,
}
```

### struct `Awaits`

The await store: one JSON record per pending wake under `~/.adi/mono/awaits`. Cheap to clone — all state is on disk, like every other store here.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Awaits {
    config: Config,
}
```

### struct `Request`

What a run asked for, before it becomes a stored `Await`. The tool builds one of these from the model's arguments; `register` is what turns it into a record.

```rust
    pub after_seconds: Option<u64>,

    pub check: Option<String>,
    pub expires_in_seconds: Option<u64>,
    pub cwd: String,
}
```

```rust
    id: String,
```

### struct `ToolResult`

What running one call produced. `ok` false is a tool that failed, which is an answer the model is expected to read and act on — not a failure of the turn.

```rust
struct ToolResult {
    call_id: String,
    name: String,
    output: String,
    ok: bool,
}
```

### struct `Reply`

One round-trip's outcome, in provider-neutral terms.

```rust
struct Reply {
    text: String,
    calls: Vec<ToolCall>,
    raw: Value,
    input_tokens: Option<u64>,
    output_tokens: Option<u64>,
}
```

### enum `Wire`

A provider's tool-calling dialect: how the conversation starts, how one round is sent and read, and how a round plus its tool results is appended for the next one.

```rust
enum Wire<'a> {
    Anthropic {
        args: &'a HarnessAdiArguments,
        model: &'a str,
    },
    OpenAi {
        args: &'a HarnessAdiArguments,
        model: &'a str,
        dialect: &'static OpenAiDialect,
    },
    Gemini {
        args: &'a HarnessAdiArguments,
        model: &'a str,
    },
    Ollama {
        args: &'a HarnessAdiArguments,
        model: &'a str,
    },
}
```

### struct `OpenAiDialect`

The two providers that speak `OpenAI`'s `/v1/chat/completions`. They agree on the whole request body but disagree on where they live, which variable holds the key, and — the one that bites — what the output cap is called.

```rust
struct OpenAiDialect {
    provider: &'static str,
    default_base: &'static str,
    default_key_env: &'static str,
    max_tokens_field: &'static str,
    default_max_tokens: u64,
}
```


`adi.agents.run.deleted` — one run of an agent was deleted outright: it was stopped if still live, and its log, metadata and any transcript are gone. Distinct from `stopped`, which ends a run but leaves it in the history to read.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct AgentRunDeleted {
    pub agent: String,
    pub run_id: String,
}
```

## `src/limits.rs`

### struct `RunLimits`

The `sessions/settings.toml` shape: how many runs may be live at once, overall and per project. Unknown fields are ignored, so an older store keeps loading.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct RunLimits {
    pub max_concurrent_runs: u32,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    pub projects: BTreeMap<String, u32>,
}
```

### struct `RunLoad`

What is running right now: the total, and how it divides between projects. Taken in one pass so a launch, a poll, or a page render weighs both caps without walking the store twice.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RunLoad {
    total: usize,
    by_project: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
}
```

## `src/memo.rs`

### struct `Stamp`

A file's identity: two cheap `stat` fields that together change whenever its bytes do.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Stamp {
    len: u64,
    modified: SystemTime,
}
```

### struct `Entry`

One remembered parse, plus when it was last handed out (for eviction).

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Entry<T> {
    stamp: Stamp,
    value: Arc<T>,
    used: u64,
}
```

### struct `Memo`

A bounded map from file path to its parsed contents.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Memo<T> {
    entries: Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, Entry<T>>>,
    tick: AtomicU64,
    capacity: usize,
}
```

## `src/progress.rs`

### enum `Step`

One item on a turn's timeline, in the order the engine emitted it.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Step {
    Message {
        text: String,
    },
    Thinking {
        text: String,
    },
    Tool {
        name: String,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
        input: String,
        status: ToolStatus,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
        output: String,
    },
}
```

### enum `ToolStatus`

A tool step's lifecycle: still running, finished ok, or failed.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ToolStatus {
    Running,
    Ok,
    Error,
}
```

### struct `TurnMetrics`

Per-turn telemetry from the engine's final event. Cost is kept in micro-dollars (integer) so the whole model stays `Eq` — the poll-change comparisons and jsonl round-trips depend on it.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TurnMetrics {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub input_tokens: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub output_tokens: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub cost_micro_usd: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub duration_ms: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub num_turns: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub permission_denials: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]
    pub is_error: bool,
}
```

### struct `TurnContent`

A turn/run's parsed content: the answer text, its activity steps, and its metrics.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TurnContent {
    pub text: String,
    pub steps: Vec<Step>,
    pub metrics: Option<TurnMetrics>,
}
```

### struct `BackendCapabilities`

What a backend can surface — the single source of truth the API reports and the UI renders from, consolidating the old ad-hoc interactive/answerable flags with the new progress features.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BackendCapabilities {
    pub interactive: bool,
    pub history: bool,
    pub answerable: bool,
    pub live_text: bool,
    pub tool_steps: bool,
    pub thinking: bool,
    pub metrics: bool,
}
```

## `src/run.rs`

### enum `Launch`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Launch {
    Pty {
        command: String,
        session: String,
    },
    Process {
        command: String,
        pid: u32,
        log: PathBuf,
        run_id: String,
    },
}
```

### enum `Sent`

What became of a message said into a conversation. One turn runs at a time, so a message sent while the agent is still answering is not refused — it takes its place in the queue and starts when the current answer lands.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Sent {
    Started(Launch),
    Queued {
        place: usize,
    },
}
```

### struct `Peek`

A read-only snapshot of one run for the live view: the visible output (a pty screen capture, or the tail of a detached run's log — which persists after the run ends), whether it is still live, a human attach/tail hint, and whether the backend is interactive (only an interactive one can be typed into).

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Peek {
    pub running: bool,
    pub output: String,
    pub attach: String,
    pub interactive: bool,
}
```

### struct `RunInfo`

One entry in a headless agent's run history. The agent definition is only a template: each Run spawns an independent run from those settings (a fresh dialog, never continuing a prior one), keeps its own log, and several may be live at once. Newest-first ordering is the caller's job.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RunInfo {
    pub run_id: String,
    pub started_at: u64,
    pub last_activity: u64,
    pub message: String,
    pub running: bool,
    pub hidden: bool,
}
```

### struct `Pane`

A live pane, addressed by the agent that owns it and nothing else.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Pane {
    agent: String,
    log: PathBuf,
}
```

## `src/runner/detached.rs`

### struct `DetachedRunner`

A headless run of one engine: spawn a detached child, watch its pid, read its log.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DetachedRunner {
    backend: Backend,
}
```

### struct `State`

What this runner keeps about a session: the child it started, and the engine session that child established. Nothing else — everything durable is the store's.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct State {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pid: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    session_id: Option<String>,
}
```

### struct `Cursor`

How far into the log a reader has got, and whether it has already been told the run ended.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Cursor {
    #[serde(default)]
    offset: u64,
    #[serde(default)]
    finished: bool,
}
```

### struct `Stopped`

What a `Runner::stop` found and did. `forced` says the grace period ran out and the runner had to be rude about it — worth recording, since a run that never exits cooperatively is a fact about the engine rather than about the click that stopped it.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Stopped {
    pub was_running: bool,
    pub forced: bool,
}
```

## `src/store/transcript.rs`

### struct `Turn`

One message in a session's transcript.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Turn {
    pub role: String,
    pub text: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub at: u64,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]
    pub pending: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]
    pub queued: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]

    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub metrics: Option<TurnMetrics>,
}
```

### struct `At`

Just the moment off a turn's line. A listing asks when a conversation last spoke, not what it said, and everything else on the line — a whole answer, and every tool call that produced it — is skipped rather than built.

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct At {
    #[serde(default)]
    at: u64,
}
```
